When ordering after taking a seat, you can choose the type of puffer fish (silver or puffer fish) and then order whether it is spicy (clear soup) or spicy (spicy soup).
I ate Eunbok Guk (Jiri).
It's 12,000 won.
I think it's a bit overpriced for lunch, but when you try it, you'll nod your head.
Chambok soup costs 18,000 won, but I haven’t tried it. Haha
A lot of people visit here during lunch time, so if you visit after 11:30, you will have to wait.
We recommend that you visit before 11:30 or after 12:30.
Among the basic side dishes that are set after ordering, they provide seasoned pufferfish skin, which is a delicacy.
They made wasabi and soy sauce sauce, and when you eat seasoned pufferfish, they bring you puffer fish soup. If you eat a spoonful of water parsley and soup, ugh... I don't even drink yesterday, but I feel like I'm having a hangover.
The person who ate with me said that it felt like spring was a treat.
If you take a bite of the puffer fish, fillet it, and dip it in wasabi and soy sauce, your mouth will enjoy it.
Despite the price of this restaurant being a little too high for my standards, I would like to recommend that you visit this restaurant at least once every three months.
The food is clean and delicious.
I give it 4.7 out of 5.
If you can afford it, I also recommend fried pufferfish.
Today I got some and ate pufferfish fritters.. 👍

A restaurant full of Blue Ribbon Survey stickers. Shandong Gyoza next to the Chinese Embassy in Myeongdong. Beneath the blue ribbon is the sign of Heo Young-man and John Lee, as it was the house that appeared in Baekban Travels. Five-spice soybean pork and water dumplings were featured on the broadcast. I heard that it appeared in Sung Si-kyung's Something to Eat, and it has become incredibly popular since then. A house where there was a long line of people waiting in the evening.

The name of the fried meat menu is Tempura. This is also half the large size. 29,000 won. Because it is fried pork, it looks like sweet and sour pork. I haven't tried this restaurant's sweet and sour pork, but the fried pork is firmer and crispier than regular sweet and sour pork. The texture was too much for my mouth as I don't enjoy solid food.

Half of chive japchae (large). 50,000 won. It's more expensive than I thought. Metallurgy It is good to settle down. It is called seasonal menu.

Water dumplings are a signature menu item along with five-spice soybean pork. Multiply 12,000 won. They look crooked as if they were handmade dumplings. It was a delicacy to eat it with sour five-spice sauce.

#Myeongdong #Haenghwachon

“A model of burnt Uni Jjajangmyeon”

Haenghwachon’s Jjajangmyeon is one of my favorite Jjajangmyeon.
This is the well-balanced, hexagonal Jjajangmyeon that we used to eat in the old days.

I have liked this place for a long time, so much so that my review was the first of Haenghwachon, and it is said that the popularity of this place has soared recently after it appeared on Seong Si-kyung's Mukten.
Somehow, there were too many customers compared to before...

Since tasting Haenghwachon Jjajangmyeon for the first time almost 10 years ago, I visit this restaurant once every 1-2 years to eat Jjajangmyeon, and the taste has hardly changed.
It maintains its original taste both now and then.

The Jjajangmyeon here is Uni Jjajang, the basis of burnt Jjajangmyeon.
It's not a sloppy water jjajang that's been treated with starch because it's thin, but there's quite a bit of onion and meat in it, so it feels like a well-made ragu.

It has the taste of chunjang (chunjang), sweetness, and umami, plus the unique scent of Haenghwachon.
The mixing properties with the noodles are good, and even the viscosity of the paste that comes with the noodles is ideal.

It's a shame that the noodles are a bit dry, but the sauce is delicious, so that's it.
Moreover, if you get this delicious Jjajangmyeon for 6,000 won in Myeongdong, it's not a waste to give it a perfect score.

2024.4.13. Saturday visit

It's been a while since I visited, and something has changed a bit.

1) Serving robot
A robot carries food and empty dishes. When the robot arrives at the table, the waiter puts the food on the table.

2) Kimchi
In the past, we used to give each person a plate of kimchi, but now they only give one per table. Instead, it is served in a stainless steel bowl and the amount is larger than before.

3) Rice
They used to give as much rice as needed, but now they only give one bowl per person.

4) Xylitol gum
The xylitol gum that was given with meal tickets when paying in advance is no longer provided.

Other than that, as is common in popular restaurants, the well-organized system where employees work hand in hand with each other, Myeongdong Gyoza's unique kalguksu and kimchi taste, and very friendly employees have remained the same as before.

After the coronavirus outbreak, foreigners returned to Myeongdong, and it seems that Koreans don't visit Myeongdong often anymore. However, there are still a few old restaurants in Myeongdong that are still firmly standing, and Myeongdong Gyoza is one of them. In Myeong-dong, there are more and more places doing business like gangsters, and with Chinese capital infiltrating, these restaurants seem to be in trouble. reviews.author: Chanwook Lee
reviews.text:
Chinese franchise companies are expanding their presence in the Korean market day by day, and it is no exaggeration to say that Haidilao is at the forefront. What special secret is hidden in Haidarao Hot Pot?

Hai Di Lao in Korea is all directly managed and has branches in every downtown area in Seoul, and I visited the Myeong-dong branch, which takes the stance of the main branch. As expected, there were many foreign guests, especially Chinese.

Most of the staff seemed to be from China, and although communication was not smooth, they put a lot of effort into serving customers. Since it was my first visit, I asked a lot of questions and chose four soups.

You can make the hot pot sauce yourself at the self-service bar, but a 3,500 won fee per person is charged. In fact, it could be considered a sauce-only self-serve bar, with the exception of a few side dishes and fruits, and was mainly composed of sauces.

I made the sauce based on a lot of recipes circulating on the Internet, and as I experienced in Chongqing, the key ingredients are sesame oil, minced garlic, and peanut sauce. If you decide to make your soup spicy, you need to make the sauce a little heavier.

The ingredients for the soup are set when you order them on a tablet, but the prices are generally not cheap. Still, I ordered plenty of thinly sliced ​​pork belly, beef pork belly, tofu skin, duck intestine tea, shrimp balls, and various vegetables.

Looking at the soup and ingredients ordered, among the various flavors of mala, the spicy level was cheongyu mala, which was level 3. It was less greasy and cleaner than Chongqing hot pot, which is based on beef fat, but at the same time, it did not lack a bland taste.

It wasn't spicy or not spicy, but I thought it would be okay to go to level 5 unless it was too soft and you wouldn't want to eat it by the spoonful. The subtle sweetness and coolness of brewing with green onions was well absorbed by the ingredients and went best with duck intestines.

I was secretly looking forward to the sum chai stew, a pickled cabbage stew, similar to the sum chai stew I had in Chongqing, but of course it does not contain freshwater fish. It was made with just pickled cabbage and peppers, so it was only sour and slightly cool, and had no depth.

It was a soup that went well with vegetables rather than meat, and went especially well with tofu skin. The tofu skin added oil and flavor, and the texture of the soup soaking up the soup and loosening up was quite impressive.

As a matter of courtesy, I ended up with three vegetables: enoki mushrooms, cabbage, and bean sprouts, but as I ate it, I felt it was closer to shabu-shabu than hot pot. There was chicken on the bottom of the samgyetang hot pot, and it tasted like a whole chicken.

Even though thinly sliced ​​pork belly and beef pork belly don't have the texture of duck intestines, they're not hardcore and don't smell, so they're not bad options. The staff made the shrimp balls and it was nice that the shrimp were firm.

I ran out of ingredients to put in the soup, so I tried adding cotton tofu and lamb, but the lamb wasn't as good as not using it. It had a very musty sheep smell, the texture was tough, and the seasoning did not absorb well even after being soaked in the soup for a long time.

The cotton tofu had a light texture similar to fish cake, so it was edible, and both were dipped in tomato soup. However, the tomato stew had too much of a fusion feel to it, so I wasn't attracted to it.

Looking back, there was no need to order four soups, and it would have been more satisfying to save money by ordering two or three more ingredients. Anyway, I finished my order with the side menu of meat and fried flower bread.

The fried meat was only 5,000 won, and it was seasoned well and thickly fried, making it a good cost-effective snack to wash off any leftover alcohol. I thought it was a waste of money to buy the fried flower bread, but when it came out, I dipped it in condensed milk and enjoyed it.

I visited Haidilao for the first time in my life because I missed Chongqing and hot pot. The biggest advantages can be summarized as stable taste and excellent customer service. However, there is no doubt that the price of hot pot is somewhat excessively premium.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Myeongdong #Din Tai Fung

“Din Tai Fung is not being rewritten.”

It's been a while since Din Tai Fung came to Korea, but I still blindly believe that our country's Din Tai Fung is the most delicious Din Tai Fung in the world.

When I visited last year, I thought Din Tai Fung in Myeongdong had improved in terms of food and service, but this return visit clearly reminded me that, as the old saying goes, Din Tai Fung cannot be changed.

Even though I liked it a lot, Xiaolongpo is not as thick and juicy as the foreign Din Tai Fung.
The other foods are just as tasty and good as you can get at a regular franchise Chinese restaurant, but they are expensive.
When it comes to food, there isn't much development or appeal.

Then, is the service at least good?
There weren't that many customers, but ordering was difficult in a group room.
It took more than 30 minutes to order a bottle of Yantae Goryangju, and I had to beg four different servers to get it, but they couldn't help me, so I went along and got it.
It seems that no one has any “responsibility” to fulfill the requests they receive.

Moreover, the servers at least make them know what their menu is and use them as part-time workers, so they are no different from robots as restaurant workers.

The vagueness of the corkage policy is also a problem.
Last year, I used it well because it was a corkage-free business, but this year, no matter how much I look at the headquarters website or apps like Kete, there is no clear explanation about corkage.
After calculating it later, I think I got about 30,000 won per bottle.
Of course, they don't tell you when calculating, so I'm not sure.

It has no taste
The service is terrible
Korea’s Din Tai Fung, whose information is lacking in accuracy!

It was once again confirmed that Din Tai Fung is the worst in the world.

#Ruscious's Worst

reviews.author: Eyedaq Optical Shop Myeong-dong
reviews.text:
‘Mappa Sacheon Ttukbaegi Restaurant’, newly opened in the middle of Myeong-dong, is a casual Chinese restaurant that brings out the spicy flavor of Szechuan style in a Korean style ttukbaegi. The location is 13 Myeongdong 7-gil, Jung-gu, 1st floor of Myeongdong Securities Building (Myeongdong 1-ga). It is within walking distance of Euljiro Entrance and Myeongdong Station, so accessibility is good.

The signature items, as the name suggests, include mapo tofu in an earthen pot, Sichuan red beef (hongxiaorou), and spicy earthenware with a lively marinara flavor. Based on SNS and visit reviews, the soup is served boiling, so it is good to mix with rice, and many say that it has a distinct scent of sancho and red pepper oil, but is not overly oily. The spicy level is quite spicy even at ‘normal’ level, so a tip is to ask for the spiciness to be adjusted. For 2-3 people, the combination of mapo tofu + red beef + rice or earthen pot + sides is good value for money.

As the store is newly opened, it has a clean interior and quick turnover. It is crowded with office workers during lunch and shoppers in the evening, so waiting may occur during peak times. Business hours and last orders are subject to change, so it is safe to check using a map app or phone before visiting. There are many beer bars and cafes nearby, so it is easy to find a secondary route.

I ordered Jjambbong, and the people I visited with me ordered crab fried rice. I was satisfied with it, but one of the people who ordered crab fried rice said it was delicious, while another said it was so-so.

The only thing I can't help but rate the service low is that there is a system in which orders are placed through a kiosk and a female employee serving the food takes the issued order form and then brings the food, but the female employee is not our person and communication is not smooth.
And he committed the atrocity(?) of delivering Jjamppong first to another table who came later than me and ordered it...
Additionally, this restaurant starts cooking once an order is placed, so the food comes out later compared to other Chinese restaurants.
So we concluded that people were lining up because the table turnover rate was low.
Of course, I'm not saying the food isn't delicious, the food tastes okay.
If I visit next time, I will choose Jjamppong Rice.
Regarding store accessibility, I think it would be good to visit on days when the weather is bad because it is located midway between Euljiro 1-ga Station and Euljiro 3-ga Station on Line 2 (Euljiro 2-ga).
It's not a restaurant worth visiting from far away, but I think it's good value for money for Jjambbong. Fried rice was 8,000 won.

reviews.author: Lee Seong-gil
reviews.text:
Around 2017, I came to know about this house for the first time when I started working nearby.
At that time, I occasionally ate meals with the employees at this place, and it was a pretty good memory....
I recently started working near here again, so I decided to visit.

First of all, it is basically seen as a standard for judging the quality of a Chinese restaurant, and my personal favorite is Ganjjajang, so I went to eat Ganjjajang.

[August 9th] I visited and had to have a late lunch because I was on a business trip.
There were three teams in the restaurant, including me, with one person each.
I was about to take a seat, but the woman at the counter told me to sit somewhere else.
I sat down at the seat he assigned me and ordered soybean paste...
The food came out about 20 minutes later. -_-;
As I wrote above, it was a late lunch, so there were only three people (including me) in the restaurant.

[August 21st] On this day, I also visited for a late lunch.
I was about to take a seat, but the woman at the counter told me to sit somewhere else, so I sat somewhere else.
I don't remember the customers well, but I think there were about 2 teams (2 people).
This time, I also ordered Ganjjajang and it took about 15 minutes before the food came out.
I took a bite and felt that the taste was a little different from before.

[October 3] This time, it was late because I was on a business trip, so I couldn't think of a good place near the office where I could eat quickly and go to the office, so I visited again.
I was about to take a seat, but the woman at the counter told me to sit somewhere else, so I sat somewhere else.
There were two guests including me.
I also ordered Ganjjajang and turned on the stopwatch based on my previous experience.
This time, surprisingly, the food came out at an astonishing speed of 4 minutes and 31 seconds.
The moment I mixed it well and took a bite, a taste of oil filled my mouth.
yes?? I tried to taste the jjajang by chewing it, but it tasted like everything was covered in oil.
Haha... I ate a little bit before leaving.
I thought I should never come again.

[November 6th] I thought about not coming here again, but I still had to quickly finish my late lunch and go to the office, so I consoled myself and visited again.
I was about to take a seat, but the woman at the counter told me to sit somewhere else, so I sat somewhere else.
There were 3 guests including me.
This time, based on my previous experience, I did not order Ganjjajang.
Because I felt like it was going to get worse.
They even put up a sign outside advertising their seasonal menu item, Oyster Jjamppong, so I ordered Oyster Jjamppong.
I know that this place used to be famous for jjambbong, but as of 2024, it seems like only the fame remains.
It was just oyster jjambbong, there was no taste whatsoever and the oysters were bland as if they had not yet tasted good.
The soup had a slightly oyster-related taste, and anyone who asked could just say it was oyster jjamppong and couldn't recommend it.

Normally, if the personality isn't good, I just pass it on and write a review, but that's not the case.
Well, wouldn't it be okay if the taste was serious enough to harm the health of the guests?
So, on my third visit, I decided to just not come again, but due to my lapse in judgment, I got angry on my fourth visit.

First: How the woman who manages the hall operates
I always went for a late lunch because of work, and it was usually around 2 o'clock.
There were about 14 tables in the hall and there were about 3 teams when I visited.
If so, there will be 11 remaining tables, and due to time constraints, it is very unlikely that groups will come.
However, the moment I sit down, they always tell me to sit somewhere else.
why?? Are there any group guests coming?? He is very busy training his dog.

The tone of voice, honed over years of experience, is perfectly disguised as friendliness.
When I first heard it, I thought he was a very kind person! Anyone can fall into this illusion.
However, if you listen closely to the words of kindness coming out of his mouth, you will be able to make a better judgment about your own situation.
Her eyes do not stay at the guests' dining tables.

Second: I heard that the chef is the owner, but the food varies greatly.
It's harder to see a store fail with the owner in the kitchen, but I think I've finally found it.

I was so angry that I wrote it focusing on the shortcomings, but it's not all there are.
I heard a phone order came from the hall, but it was from someone who seemed to be a regular who works nearby.
I ordered a bowl of Jjambbong and it was delivered!

Outside this building, there are two delivery motorcycles standing.
Originally, a Chinese restaurant that provides its own delivery service had no choice but to be recognized as a restaurant.
So I came back to this house, but in my case, it ended in great failure.

I remembered that there was a line outside the building in 2017, but when I thought about it again, I suddenly remembered that it wasn't like that at all these days.
I think there are probably a lot of people who have had similar experiences to what I experienced above.

If so, it can be said that it has naturally entered the path of decline, but I am writing this review to provide some help to people who plan to visit this place in the future due to its popularity.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
Wonheung is a Chinese restaurant quietly located in an alley in Dadong, Jung-gu.
The location is strange, so when you first look for it, you might be confused as to whether you've come to the right place, but when you open the door and enter, the Chinese spoken back and forth immediately sets the mood.

The store is not large and has only a few tables, so even when I went for an open run before lunch on a Saturday, it was more than half full.
It feels like it will definitely be more crowded on weekdays.
The menu items that stood out were jjamppong and fried meat, and almost every table was eating these two.

Since I was visiting alone, I only focused on the fried meat.
I ordered the smallest medium dish, but the price was quite high at 33,000 won, and the quantity was surprisingly not that much.
Compared to a whole chicken, pork parts will be much cheaper, but you may be a little disappointed in terms of quantity and price.

But as soon as I took a bite, I realized why this restaurant is famous for its fried meat.
The batter was fluffy rather than crispy, but not too thick, so the meat didn't get soggy and was soft all the way through without any unpleasant smell.
It is a combination that you eat with soy sauce rather than a separate sauce. Surprisingly, you don't get tired even if you keep eating it.

However, since the menu was monotonous and the price was too high to fill one's stomach with just one of these meat fries, I thought it would be much more beneficial to go with two or more people and share several menu items.
I also want to try a proper meal with jjambbong next time.
The jjamppong I was eating at the table next to me was so delicious that I regretted not ordering it.

First of all, the presence of the building is huge from the exterior. It's advertised brilliantly. There are shops themed around various countries within the building, and it is decorated with the concept of going on a trip from the airport. I visited during the day, but I liked the atmosphere so I also visited at night. For the menu, I had Dongpo Pork Rice Bowl, Wonton Noodles, Dongling Tea (凍檸茶), and Mid-Level Toast.

1. Dongpo Pork Rice Bowl
It lacked the feel of Dongpoyuk. It doesn't have a soft feel, and the sauce doesn't taste like dongpo meat. There isn't enough bok choy. It would have been good enough if the sauce had been done well... But it's okay if you add chili oil.

2. Dongling tea (凍檸茶)
I also tried it at a Hong Kong-style cafe in COEX, and they use lemon nyeong (檸) in their name! I didn't know before because I wasn't interested, but I looked up how to write Dongling tea in Chinese characters and learned about it.

3. Mid-Levels Toast
This toast is named after the Mid-Levels Escalator from Chungking Express. It was too sweet for me, but I still imagined Hong Kong in the movie while eating the sweet toast. The Hong Kong of the 1990s, which I have never been to and cannot go to.

4. Wonton noodles
I visited in the evening. The shrimp are plump and delicious. Because it contains a lot of green onions, it neutralizes the taste that can be greasy. I recommend eating it on a cold day.

It's also a lot of fun to look around the interior. I visited in the evening and added a few more photos. It is also decorated with neon signs and mahjong. On one wall, it says "I love you for 10,000 years." There were posters all over the stairs, and there was even an autograph from Editor-in-Chief Joo Seong-cheol. I read a book written by this person about pilgrimage to Hong Kong film locations.
The floor is also tiled, but it feels sticky every time I walk on it. I thought, ‘This feels like Hong Kong too.’ (I heard that the humidity in Hong Kong is very high, but I don't know much. I haven't been to Hong Kong yet.)
It's not a quiet style store. There is an exciting song playing in Chinese. In the evening, quiet songs are played. I wanted to eat quietly while listening to the Chongqing Express OST, but it was impossible.

reviews.author: Choi Yoo-jeong
reviews.text:
The food comes out quickly so it would be a good place to visit for lunch!!
The food is really delicious too haha
You must try the levitating noodles. I highly recommend it.
